scope: Art direction v2 motion test (24.7 s): the approved style frames in motion with the episode's own narration (c03_03-05, c03_10) and captions

beat.narration: But beneath the rising stock prices, many businesses were struggling.

shots.understanding: The market is climbing while the company underneath is burning through cash, kept alive by money piped in from investors.
shots.focal_point: BigCart's building (left third); the rising TECH STOCKS board at the vanishing point is the secondary read
shots.camera: one slow dolly toward BigCart's lobby (scale 1.0->1.09, sky layer 1.025, foreground passes faster: 3-layer parallax)
shots.lighting: dusk key from the end of the street, lamp pools breathing slightly, haze, grade

graphics.why: rising stock prices shown where the street sees them

graphics.what: gold glints flowing through the capital pipe into BigCart
graphics.why: investor money is the input keeping the firm alive

graphics.what: furnace chimney smoke with gold embers thickens on 'struggling'; lobby cash tank drains
graphics.why: the episode's cash-furnace metaphor: money burns faster than it earns

graphics.what: 'BigCart.com and Summit Ventures are fictional companies' tag
graphics.why: required disclosure: fictional companies must be labelled on screen

shots.rationale: Establishing places the relationship (investors -> company) and the contradiction (rising market vs struggling firm) before any explanation. The founder walking into BigCart introduces the person the close-up returns to.

beat.narration: They were spending heavily on advertising, employees and infrastructure without earning enough revenue to sustain themselves. Their survival depended on investors continuing to provide capital.

shots.understanding: Spending (ads, staff, servers) far exceeds revenue; the difference is investor cash, so the company only survives while investors keep paying.
shots.focal_point: the whiteboard diagram, with the manager (the founder) pointing at each part as it is named
shots.camera: opens slightly wide on the team, settles onto the board as the explanation starts, then pushes to the gap on 'investors'
shots.lighting: office panels + warm dusk window light, soft shadows, mild fog

graphics.what: SPENDING stack builds ADS / STAFF / SERVERS on 'advertising' / 'employees' / 'infrastructure'
graphics.why: each cost lands on its word

graphics.what: short REVENUE column on 'revenue', circled on 'sustain'
graphics.why: the shortfall is visible, then emphasised

graphics.what: dashed level line on 'depended', gold INVESTOR CASH block fills the gap on 'investors'
graphics.why: explains the mechanism: investors fund the gap
proportions are illustrative, not sourced figures

shots.rationale: A medium shot carries explanation and reaction together: the diagram is drawn by a character in the world (no floating dashboard), and the team's reactions (hand to forehead on 'without earning enough') carry the stakes. Background life (typing, a phone call, a carton of BigCart merchandise carried past on 'advertising') answers the 'empty office' critique.

beat.narration: Without fresh capital, they could no longer finance their operations.

shots.understanding: When the investor money stops, the company cannot pay to operate: the cash line hits bottom, the runway reaches zero, the office goes dark.
shots.focal_point: the founder's face; the CRT in the right third carries the data
shots.camera: locked off with a 3.5% push — stillness for the emotional beat
shots.lighting: red CRT key flickering on his face, cool fill, blurred night office with its last lights

graphics.what: cash line completes its fall on 'no longer'; RUNWAY LEFT counts 3 -> 0 months on 'finance'
graphics.why: the consequence, on the object he is looking at

graphics.what: office lights behind him go out on 'operations'
graphics.why: operations ending, shown as an environmental action

shots.rationale: The close-up turns the mechanism into consequence. Acting is restrained and readable at this size: brows knit on 'without fresh capital', eyelids grow heavy on 'no longer', the phone comes down on 'finance', the head drops on 'operations'. Kinetic typography was considered and rejected here: the captions and the CRT already carry the words, and the guide says not to duplicate captions on screen.
